items.quote: Yousef used the program, Google Earth , on his computer
items.text: Yousef used the program, Google Earth, on his computer to study the geography of Egypt. Yousef noticed some green, circular areas next to the desert areas so, he asked his father about them.

items.quote: Yousef noticed some green, circular areas

items.quote: The father Said: You learn that a drop of water
items.text: The father Said: You learn that a drop of water means the source of life. Therefore, we should minimize the consumption of water in order to irrigate the land by the central irrigation method (sprinkle irrigation) in which, the wheels of the irrigation machine circle around a fixex point which draws those circles.

items.quote: is the set of points of a plane which are at constant distance from a fixed point
items.claim: The circle is the set of points of a plane which are at constant distance from a fixed point in the same plane.

items.quote: The fixed point is called the centre of the circle
items.claim: The fixed point is called the centre of the circle and the constant distance is called the radius length.

items.quote: The circle is usually denoted by its center.
items.claim: A circle is usually denoted by its center: circle M means the circle whose center is point M.

items.stem: In the figure opposite: two concentric circles M, AB is a chord in the larger circle intersecting the smaller circle at C and D. Prove that: AC = BD.
solution: Given: AB ∩ the smaller circle = {C, D}
items.notes: Solution continues on next page; no final answer on this page.

items.quote: two concentric circles M
items.caption: Two concentric circles with centre M; chord BA of larger circle meets smaller circle at D and C; E is the foot of the perpendicular from M to the chord (right angle at E, dotted segment). Points B, D, E, C, A in order on the chord.

items.quote: Construction : Draw ME ⊥ AB to intersect it at E
items.text: Construction: Draw $\overline{ME} \perp \overline{AB}$ to intersect it at E.

items.quote: By subtracting (2) from (1), we get:
items.text: Proof: In the larger circle $\overleftrightarrow{ME} \perp \overline{AB}$, so $EA = EB$ (1) (corollary). In the smaller circle $\overleftrightarrow{ME} \perp \overline{CD}$, so $EC = ED$ (2) (corollary). By subtracting (2) from (1), we get: $EA - EC = EB - ED$, so $\therefore AC = BD$ (Q.E.D.)
items.notes: Continuation of the proof begun on previous page; the page prints the Construction and Proof lines only.

learning_objectives.label: Basic circle terms and radii
learning_objectives.description: Identify and use the basic terms of the circle (centre, radius, chord, diameter, surface of the circle, points inside, on and outside) and use radii and diameters to compare lengths and solve problems.

learning_objectives.label: Axes of symmetry in circle
learning_objectives.description: Describe the axes of symmetry of a circle and state that any straight line through the centre is an axis of symmetry.

learning_objectives.label: Chord–centre perpendicular corollaries
learning_objectives.description: Apply the corollaries relating the centre, a chord and its midpoint or perpendicular to calculate lengths, angles and areas and to prove statements about chords.
